rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off_track with zero finishes. Progress was only 0.11 to 0.20, rms_error 0.019 to 0.032 and max_error about 0.06 to 0.067, which is at or past the off-track limit of 0.06 m. Steering_oscillation of 0.11 to 0.16 and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run point to an over-aggressive loop that overshoots and then loses the tape, not to a slow loop. The current kp of 3.0 with weights up to +/-2 gives a turn of up to 6, or about 2100 PWM of differential, which is very likely the cause. The sensor cluster of 0.04 m is also narrow relative to the 0.025 m tape, so the signal changes sharply near the edge. Changes: (1) Reduce kp from 3.0 to 1.5 to halve the steering gain and cut overshoot. (2) Set ki to 0.05 to remove integral wind-up on bends. (3) Raise kd from 0.3 to 0.5 to damp the faster signal changes. (4) Spread the five sensors to x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, a 0.048 m span that covers the 25 mm tape with margin so the signal stays linear across the edge. (5) Keep base_speed at 1.5, since finishing needs about 1.5 m/s and the telemetry shows no speed-limited failure; keep wheel geometry and mass unchanged so the only changes are steering and sensing. Expected result: lower oscillation and max_error, fewer line-loss events, and a first chance at completion on the oval and s-bend. The slalom may still be marginal. The next telemetry should show whether the drop in kp reduced max_error below 0.06.
